¿Cómo se predice la geometría de una mol: How do you predict the geometry of a molecule with VSEPR?
Los pares de electrones del átomo centra: The electron pairs of the central atom repel each other and place themselves as far apart as possible: 2 pairs, linear (180°); 3, trigonal planar (120°); 4, tetrahedral (109.5°); 5, trigonal bipyramidal; 6, octahedral (90°). Water has 4 pairs, 2 of them lone pairs, and is bent (≈104.5°).
¿Cómo se sabe la hibridación y si es pol: How do you know the hybridization and whether it is polar?
4 pares son sp³, 3 son sp² y 2 son sp. U: 4 pairs are sp³, 3 are sp² and 2 are sp. A molecule is polar if the dipoles of its bonds do not cancel: CO₂ (linear) is nonpolar and H₂O (bent) is polar.

En la estructura de Lewis cada enlace es: In the Lewis structure each bond is a shared pair of electrons and each lone pair is drawn as two dots. To distribute the electrons: add the valence e⁻ (subtracting the charge if it is an anion and adding it if it is a cation), join the terminal atoms to the central one with single bonds, complete the octets of the terminals and the remaining pairs go to the central atom.
La <b>carga formal</b> C<sub>f</sub> es: The formal charge Cf is V (valence electrons of the free atom) minus P (electrons in lone pairs) minus E/2 (half the bonding electrons). The best structure is the one with the smallest formal charges and the negative charge on the most electronegative atom. If the double bond can be moved to another identical terminal atom, there is resonance: several equivalent structures whose average is the real molecule, with an intermediate bond order (in NO₃⁻, 4/3). Atoms of period 3 or later can exceed the octet; if you check “limit to the octet” you will see the other structure, the one many books prefer for SO₂ or SO₄²⁻.
En el etanol, el ácido acético o el eten: In ethanol, acetic acid or ethene there are several “central” atoms. The geometry of each depends only on its neighbors and its lone pairs: the C of CH₃ is tetrahedral (sp³), the C of C=O is trigonal planar (sp²), the C of a triple bond is linear (sp) and the O of OH is bent (two lone pairs). A double or triple bond counts as a single domain.
La teoría de repulsión de los pares de e: Valence shell electron pair repulsion (VSEPR) theory says that the electron domains around a central atom place themselves as far from one another as possible. A domain is a bond (single, double or triple), a lone pair or an unpaired electron.
Un H o un halógeno terminal aporta 1 e⁻;: A terminal H or halogen contributes 1 e⁻; a terminal O or S joined by a double bond contributes 0.
Tipo <b>AX<sub>n</sub>E<sub>m</sub></b>:: Type AXnEm: n bonded atoms (X) and m lone pairs (E); the domains are n + m.
Un par libre ocupa más sitio que un enla: A lone pair takes up more room than a bond, and therefore closes the angles: 109.5° → 107° in NH₃ → 104.5° in H₂O.
En la bipirámide trigonal, los pares lib: In the trigonal bipyramid, lone pairs go to the equatorial plane; in the octahedron, the second lone pair goes opposite the first.
Con n dominios, el átomo central usa n o: With n domains, the central atom uses n hybrid orbitals: 2 → sp, 3 → sp², 4 → sp³, 5 → sp³d, 6 → sp³d². For 5 or more the atom must be from period 3 or later (expanded octet).
Cada enlace tiene un momento dipolar pro: Each bond has a dipole moment proportional to the electronegativity difference Δχ and points to the more electronegative atom. The molecule is polar if the vector sum of the moments is not zero: that is why CO₂ (linear) and CCl₄ (tetrahedral) are nonpolar, and H₂O and NH₃ polar.
La estructura de Lewis es para elementos: The Lewis structure is for main-group elements and molecules with all electrons paired: transition metals and radicals (odd number of electrons, such as NO or NO₂) are rejected with a warning.
Con un átomo central, los átomos de alre: With one central atom, the surrounding atoms can be H, halogens, O, S or Se. Molecules with several centers are written in condensed form and without rings.
La geometría sale del recuento de pares: The geometry comes from counting electron pairs (VSEPR): the angles are the ideal ones or the typical textbook ones when there are lone pairs (about 107° or 104.5°), not the measured angle of each molecule.
